sample_unit: patient questions (in English and French), rated by 7 experts
models_evaluated: five commercially available LLMs (not named in the abstract)

links.outcome: Readability of LLM patient education responses (Flesch–Kincaid Grade Level) versus recommended levels
links.effect: Readability analysis using the Flesch–Kincaid Grade Level indicated that responses often exceeded recommended levels for patient education.
links.quote: Readability analysis using the Flesch–Kincaid Grade Level indicated that responses often exceeded recommended levels for patient education.

links.outcome: Reading level of LLM-generated patient materials relative to recommended patient education levels
links.effect: Responses often exceeded recommended reading levels for patient education (Flesch–Kincaid Grade Level).
links.quote: Readability analysis using the Flesch–Kincaid Grade Level indicated that responses often exceeded recommended levels for patient education.

links.outcome: Expert-rated LLM accuracy, conciseness, and readability across models and languages
links.effect: LLMs performed well overall, but significant differences occurred across models and languages. Performance was generally higher in English than French. Critical errors were uncommon.
links.quote: Performance was generally higher in English, highlighting cross-lingual disparities that may affect equitable access to reliable health information.

unlisted_practices: Cross-lingual expert evaluation of LLM patient education responses for a specialized oncology therapy
Comparing domain-specific versus general-purpose LLMs for patient education

screen.reason: Expert evaluation of 5 commercial LLMs generating patient education materials in English and French, evaluating accuracy, readability, and cross-lingual disparities without directly comparing a specific deployment safeguard/practice.
